clue.text: Chief having broken eggs leaves

definitions.note: the clue gives the plural leaves; the answer names the lettuce whose leaves they are

indicators.note: to break into something is to force a way inside it, so one piece ends up within the other

blocks.note: roe is the mass of eggs in a fish
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A head chef walks out after smashing the eggs, or a boss quits in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb meaning departs, but it is the noun for salad greens, and 'broken' tells you the eggs are split open around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Romaine is the cos lettuce, a variety grown and eaten for its long crisp green foliage.

clue.text: Talk given in French, a triumph

indicators.note: something given within a stretch of text is already sitting there among its letters, waiting to be picked out

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A speech delivered in French was a great success.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across frenCH A Triumph. The French setting is a nice touch, since chat is also the French word for cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal conversation, so the noun or verb is a simple synonym for casual spoken exchange.

clue.text: E.g. mullet I had, or fishy!

indicators.note: something fishy is suspect and not as it should be, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls eating mullet, or was it some other fish?
explanation.walkthrough: Mullet and fishy steer you to the sea, but the mullet here is the haircut, short at the front and long at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullet is one particular style of haircut, so it is an example of a coiffure arrangement.

clue.text: Might one have you in a stew?

definitions.text: Might one have you in a stew?

blocks.clueFragment: Might one have you in a stew?
blocks.note: surface reading: who might get you into trouble or a state of worry?
setter's reading: someone who would literally cook you in a casserole and eat you

explanation.walkthrough: To be in a stew is to be agitated, and to have someone means to trouble them; read literally, the person is the meat in the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats human flesh, so such a person might quite literally put you into a stew for dinner.

clue.text: Loud sound hurt ears, initially shocking

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
a shock jolts things out of place, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A deafening noise was painful, and to the listener's ears it came as a shock at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud sound' looks like one phrase, but only 'Loud' is the definition; 'sound' goes into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderous describes a noise as booming and deafening like thunder, so it is a strong synonym for very noisy.

clue.text: Popular part of song? The opposite

blocks.note: something in is fashionable or popular
a verse is a section of a song between choruses

explanation.surface: Is the catchy bit of a song really the opposite of what we think?
explanation.walkthrough: IN for popular is a standard crossword equivalence, as in 'the in crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, an inverse is a thing reversed or contrary to another, which matches the opposite.

clue.text: Each on journey, energetically ambitious

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, so the order is reversed from the clue

blocks.note: a go is a turn or trip; to go is to journey
'a head' means each, as in tickets at five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Everyone on the trip was keen and full of drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Each = A HEAD, as in a price per person. In an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person or firm is enterprising and keen to make progress, which is a forceful, striving attitude.

clue.text: Stylish sprinting

blocks.note: first meaning: smart and attractive in a bold way
second meaning: rushing along at speed

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words suggest someone running elegantly; they are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing is an adjective for a smart, debonair look and also the present participle of dash, to run quickly.

clue.text: Updated draft of Lord’s cricket ground

indicators.note: an updated version has been revised and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revised plan for Lord's, the famous London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London home of cricket and seems to be the definition; the apostrophe-s is really 'is', and the ground is a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Trafford in Manchester is a Test match venue and home of Lancashire County Cricket Club, beside the football stadium of that name.

clue.text: Man with stapler assembled comprehensive document

indicators.note: to assemble is to put parts together into a new whole, so the letters are built into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office worker with a stapler puts together a thick report.
explanation.walkthrough: The stapler makes 'assembled' look like binding pages; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A master plan is an overall strategy setting out every stage of a project, usually written up in full.

clue.text: Born with minimum of dosh in poverty

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is the least of it, a single opening letter

blocks.note: née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone born into poverty with hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Dosh is British slang for money, which fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Need as a noun means a state of hardship and want, as in families living in need.

clue.text: Wonderful, decisive blow

blocks.note: first meaning: informally, stunning or outstanding
second meaning: a punch that ends a boxing bout

explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits two meanings that read together as praise for a great punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockout used as an adjective means sensational, and as a noun it is the punch that floors a boxer for the count.

clue.text: Editor with stash of grass — one’s hooked!

indicators.note: to stash something is to tuck it away out of sight, so one piece is hidden inside the other

blocks.note: an editor is someone who makes alterations
the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor with a hidden supply of cannabis is an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and hooked suggest drugs and addiction; grass is the plant, and 'hooked' is literal, describing the hook on top of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger for clothes has a curved hook to go over a rail, so it is a thing that is literally hooked.

clue.text: Mother’s back pecked by animal — some chicken?

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept
something pecked is taken into a beak, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A mother hen gets pecked on the back by some creature; was it a chicken?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's back' suggests MA reversed, but back here means the final letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Breast is a cut of meat from the chest of the bird, so it is one portion of a chicken.

clue.text: Onion on stick for monkey

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, so the order is reversed from the clue

blocks.note: stick means criticism, as does rap, in 'take the rap'
a scallion is a spring onion

explanation.surface: Someone holds out an onion on a stick to feed a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick is criticism here, as in 'giving someone stick', and rap is the blame or punishment. Monkey is the British word for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapscallion is a rascal or scamp, and a cheeky child is called a little monkey.

clue.text: Short of money, though secure?

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective; the answer is the past participle 'fastened'

blocks.note: first meaning: informally, broke
second meaning: held fast by a strap or belt

explanation.surface: Someone is broke yet feels safe, an odd financial paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the paradox: being hard up and being secure seem opposites, but one word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped for cash is an idiom for lacking funds, and strapped in means fastened tight with a belt.

clue.text: Horse carrying short playwright

indicators.note: whatever carries a load bears it within its grasp, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
short in height is low

explanation.surface: A horse bearing a small dramatist on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like an instruction to cut a word; it is simply a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was the Elizabethan dramatist who wrote Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine, a contemporary of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Small room, it will be accommodating small musician!

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to put them up inside, so one piece is housed within the other

blocks.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A tiny practice room that can just about fit one little performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation goes inside the pronoun rather than after it. The exclamation mark nods to the cello squeezing into a small space too.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, so the person is a particular kind of instrumental performer.

clue.text: Ring, where that woman enters fight

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a war is a fight
she is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: A boxing ring, the spot where a female fighter steps in for her bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring and fight conjure up boxing, but the ring is a flat metal disc used with a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A washer is a thin flat circle with a hole, placed under a nut or bolt head to spread the load.

clue.text: Complete appendage I got rid of

blocks.note: a fin is a limb-like part of a fish
taken as written
to shed is to cast off or get rid of

explanation.surface: A patient says they have had an extra body part entirely removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Complete looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning done or whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished is done and ready, with nothing left to add, so it means whole or concluded.

clue.text: Strand of pasta, old one cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single strand of spaghetti, rather stale, has been boiled.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooked fits the pasta picture so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a long thin ribbon of dough boiled in water, so a single piece is one length of pasta.

clue.text: Piece from Chanel, a name for style

indicators.note: a piece from something is a part taken out of it, here a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the run of letters at the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A garment from Chanel, a famous label for fashion and chic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across chanEL A Name; Chanel is the Paris fashion house, which suits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is flair and vivacious panache, so it describes a confident stylishness or dash.

clue.text: Story about Spanish gentleman not too bad?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a parable is a story with a moral
Don is the Spanish title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A tale about a Spanish nobleman: was he really so wicked?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a looser definition: something forgivable is not too bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardonable offence is excusable or forgivable, so it is minor enough to overlook.

clue.text: Large number describing a limb?

definitions.note: the clue phrase is a gloss; the answer read as an adjective means like an arm

blocks.note: first meaning: a great host
second meaning, whimsical: an adjective formed from a limb with -y added, like leggy

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is invented: adding -y makes an adjective from a noun, as with leggy or bony.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a vast crowd or multitude, and the playful made-up adjective would mean having to do with an arm.

clue.text: Brush back

blocks.note: first meaning: a broom or carpet cleaner used for sweeping
second meaning: a football defender playing behind the back line

explanation.walkthrough: Brush back reads as an instruction about hair; back is the football sense, a defensive player.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper is a cleaning tool, and in football also a defender who roams behind the other defenders.

clue.text: Smudge with slime smeared in empty bath

indicators.note: something smeared is spread about out of shape, so the letters lose their order
emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outer letters
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the letters of the word rearranged
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A mark left by gunk smeared inside a drained bathtub.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word fits the bathroom picture; the anagrammed letters go between the outside letters of the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a spot or mark that spoils a surface, much like a dirty smear.
